title: operational-signal-workflow-and-comm-templates-2026
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This document defines the Operational Signal Workflow used at Redwood Inference for turning monitoring signals into coordinated responder actions and customer communications. It includes a signal taxonomy, a step-by-step incident activation manual, an escalation matrix, a canonical runbook example, post-incident responsibilities, an on-call handoff template, a lightweight game-day scenario, and several pre-approved customer communication templates.

Audience:
- SREs, on-call engineers, incident commanders, support leads, and product owners.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API surface, Dedicated serving pools, and the control plane. Not intended for HR or purely policy escalations.

Key principles:
- Single source of truth: alerts -> incident channel -> incident doc.
- Fast acknowledgement, slow noisy escalation: set thresholds to minimize unnecessary human interrupts.
- Customer-facing clarity: status page updates within 30 minutes of incident classification.

1) Signal taxonomy (how we classify incoming events)
- SEV0: Complete service unavailability for >5 minutes impacting >50% of requests (requires incident bridge).
- SEV1: Severe degradation (e.g., p95 latency >2x SLO or error rate >5%) affecting a large subset of customers.
- SEV2: Partial degradation or one-region issue with mitigations available.
- SEV3: Minor degradation, non-urgent operational tasks, or individual customer issues.

2) Signal flow (from monitor to resolution)
1. Detection: Metric/alert systems (Prometheus alertmanager, Datadog monitors, and synthetic checks) emit a signal.
2. Alert enrichment: Alertmanager attaches runbook link, recent deployments, and relevant traces (link to x-trace).
3. Alert routing: PagerDuty receives routed alert by service tag (example: service:text-gen-api-prod).
4. Initial paging: On-call engineer receives page according to the rotation policy.
5. Acknowledge within 5 minutes: On-call acknowledges in PagerDuty and posts a one-line status in Slack incident channel #inc-text-gen-prod.
6. Triage: Run basic checks (step 4 runbook).
7. Incident classification: If SEV1/0, incident commander (IC) is designated and an incident bridge is opened, incident doc created in confluence and a status page entry draft started.
8. Recovery & mitigation: Apply rollbacks, routing changes, capacity scale-up, or circuit breakers.
9. Postmortem: Within 72 hours, responsible engineer writes a blameless postmortem; within 10 business days, it must be reviewed by the reviewers list.

3) Escalation matrix (quick reference)
| Role | Responsibility | Escalation channel | Backup |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Primary on-call (text-gen) | Triage, quick mitigation, communicate | PagerDuty -> Slack #inc-text-gen-prod | Secondary on-call
| Secondary on-call | Take over if primary is unreachable or incident complexity grows | Slack mention, escalate in PagerDuty | Duty lead
| Incident Commander (IC) | Coordinate responders, prioritize customer comms, declare severity | Incident bridge (Zoom/Jitsi), #inc-ops | SRE manager
| Duty lead / Engineering manager | Make product/rollback decisions, approve customer messaging | Phone / Slack DM | Eng director
| Customer Success Lead | Customer-facing comms & coordinate escalations with customers | Email + SalesForce case | CTO on-call

Notes: phone numbers and individual contact lines are kept in the secure oncall vault (secrets manager).

4) Canonical runbook example: "High error rate - text-generation-hosting-api"
Purpose: Steps to bring error rate back under SLO and determine root cause.
Pre-conditions: Ensure you have PagerDuty, AWS/GCP console access, and sla-role access (see infra-standards).

Immediate steps (first 15 minutes):
1. Confirm alert: open Datadog monitor, check time series, and confirm increase in 5xx or gRPC failures.
2. Check recent deploys: 
   - CLI: git log -1 --pretty=oneline origin/main
   - Deploy dashboard: go to Deployments -> service=text-gen-api and note PRs rolled out in last 30m.
3. Identify scope: run synthetic-curl against a set of golden prompts (script: scripts/check_endpoints.sh) and record response codes.
4. Check downstream dependencies: embedding-store, kv-cache, model-serving pool health. Run: ./tools/health-check --service model-pool-prod
5. If p95 latency is high, check GPU utilization: kubectl top pods -n serving | grep text-gen; if nodes at >85% GPU, proceed to scale.

Mitigation options (ordered):
- Roll back the last deployment (if matching time window) using the control-plane rollback action and mark as rollback-in-progress in the incident doc.
- Increase serving capacity: trigger autoscale policy for dedicated pools (see eng-sre/runbooks/autoscale-ops).
- Enable degraded mode: route requests to model-variant:fast-quant where acceptable (only after product owner sign-off for quality tradeoffs).
- Short-term rate limits: apply per-tenant soft quotas to reduce error amplification.

When to declare IC and bridge:
- Declare IC if the incident meets SEV1/0 or persists for >20 minutes after first mitigation attempt.

Containment checklist (for stabilization):
- [ ] Acknowledge the page in PagerDuty
- [ ] Create incident confluence doc and link in channel
- [ ] Assign roles: IC, Scribe, Tech Lead, Comms
- [ ] Publish initial status page draft (see templates below)

Recovery steps and verification:
- Confirm latency and error rates trending to baseline for at least 15 continuous minutes before declaring recovery.
- Run synthetic success jobs and validate end-to-end requests.

5) Runbook-level quick commands (examples)
- Check pods: kubectl get pods -n serving -l app=text-gen-api -o wide
- Tail logs: stern text-gen-api --namespace serving --since 20m\-g "ERROR|WARN"
- Check rolling deploys: curl -s https://deploy.internal/api/status?service=text-gen-api | jq

6) SLOs and error budget policy (quick reference)
- Service: text-generation-hosting-api (prod)
  - Availability SLO: 99.9% monthly
  - Latency SLOs: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms (in-region)
  - Error budget: 0.1% per month

Error budget burn thresholds & actions:
- 5% burn in 24h: Incident retrospective required, alert to platform reliability channel.
- 25% burn in 24h: Halt risky rollouts for the service, schedule immediate postmortem.
- 50% burn: Priority exec briefing + allocation of dedicated troubleshooting resources.

7) Status page & customer communications (automation rules)
- When to publish: A draft status message must be created within 30 minutes of IC declaration for SEV1/0; published within 60 minutes if public-impacting.
- Minimum status page fields: summary, impact, affected services, current actions, ETA for next update, link to incident doc.
- Automations: statusbot will post initial draft when incident tag is set to public-impact. Sample webhook payload (JSON):

POST /statusbot/webhook
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "incident_id": "INC-2026-0001",
  "severity": "SEV1",
  "summary": "Increased 5xx for text-generation-hosting-api",
  "affected": ["text-generation-hosting-api"],
  "created_at": "2026-02-14T14:12:00Z"
}

8) Customer comms templates (copy-paste placeholders)
Initial acknowledgement (public status):
Subject: Redwood Inference - Partial service degradation impacting text generation\nHello,

We are investigating elevated error rates impacting the text generation API. Our engineers have acknowledged the issue and are working on restoring normal service. We will post updates on this status page and in the incident doc: <CONFLUENCE-INCIDENT-URL>.

Next update by: <ETA 30m>

— Redwood Inference Trust & Ops

Status update (follow-up):
Subject: Update: text-generation API - mitigation in progress

Summary: We have identified increased load on the model-serving pool caused by a recent deploy. We are rolling back the deploy and scaling additional capacity. Error rates have decreased from 12% to 4%. Recovery ETA: ~25 minutes.

Customer-facing resolution (final):
Subject: Resolved: text-generation service restored

Summary: The service has recovered after rollback to commit <SHA> and scaling serving capacity. No data loss was observed. If you experienced errors during the incident, please open a support case referencing INC-<ID>.

9) Post-incident & learning loop
- Within 24 hours: IC posts initial incident timeline and provisional causes in confluence doc.
- Within 72 hours: Primary author drafts the postmortem using the template below.
- Within 10 business days: Review meeting with SRE, product, and customer success to validate remediation actions and owner assignment.

Postmortem minimum template (copy into confluence)
- Title: [SEV] Short title - YYYY-MM-DD
- Summary: 2–3 sentence blameless summary
- Impact: services/customers affected, times, measurable impact
- Timeline: minute-level timeline with commands & links
- Root cause analysis: evidence-backed cause(s)
- Action items: owner, ETA, verification steps
- Follow-ups: customer outreach tasks, docs to update

10) On-call handoff & rotation notes
Handoff checklist:
- Declare handoff in Slack with day-summary and known issues
- Share current incidents and link to the confluence incident doc
- Confirm runbook bookmarks and credentials (use secrets manager)
- Confirm primary backup contact for the rotation day

Rotation guidance:
- Rotation cadence: 1-week primary rotation for SRE on-call. Secondary is 2-week shift.
- Shift swaps: require owner manager approval and update to PagerDuty schedule.

Handoff template (Slack message):
Good morning, team — handoff to @oncall-text-gen for week of YYYY-MM-DD. No active SEV incidents. Active items: 1) rollout <PR#> paused; 2) spike in synthetic errors on us-east-1 (see inc doc). Primary backup: @secondary-text-gen.

11) Game-day exercise (lightweight scenario, 90 minutes)
Objective: Validate detection, automated mitigations, IC appointment, and status page publication.
Participants: 1 IC, 2 responders, 1 scribe, 1 comms owner.
Scenario: Synthetic monitor simulates a 6-minute SEV1 for text-generation-hosting-api caused by a model-serving OOM after a canary rollout.
Schedule:
- 0–10m: Detection & page
- 10–25m: Triage & initial mitigation (rollback)
- 25–45m: Bridge established & customer comm draft published
- 45–75m: Root cause discovery & implement longer-term fix (reproduce locally)
- 75–90m: Recovery confirmation & retrospective notes written
Success criteria:
- Acknowledge and start bridge within 10 minutes
- Status page update published within 45 minutes
- Post-exercise retro notes created within 24 hours

12) Metrics & tooling recommendations
- Monitors should include: high-cardinality error rates, synthetic end-to-end tests, model pool GPU saturation, and KV cache miss rate.
- Use the incident SDK to create incident docs automatically (inc-sdk create --service text-gen --severity SEV1).

13) Security & sensitive data handling during incidents
- Never paste full access tokens, private keys, or customer PII into incident Slack channels or confluence incident logs. Use references to secrets manager entries and redact values.

14) Appendix: quick pagerduty routing YAML sample
---
service: text-generation-hosting-api
escalation_policy: text-gen-escalation
routing_rules:
  - condition: "env == prod and severity >= SEV1"
    target: pagerduty_oncall_team_textgen
  - condition: "region == us-east-1 and severity >= SEV2"
    target: pagerduty_oncall_team_textgen_us_east
---

15) Appendix: related pages and references
- Internal deploy dashboard: https://deploy.internal/services/text-gen-api
- Incident SDK: confluence/eng-sre/incident-sdk-reference
- Autoscale ops runbook: confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/autoscale-ops

If you have suggestions for updates to this workflow or additional templates, contact the owner team: engineering@redwood-inference.internal
